A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmark study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendix A.1–A.4 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-label graph-condensation experiments in Sections 6–7, including Table 5's eight-dataset benchmark and additional analyses and experimental results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results in Table 5, adaptation experiments in Tables 2–4, and supplementary analyses and class-weighted experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The GCond, SGDD and GCDM adaptations, initialization strategies, loss functions and structure-learning procedures are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.4's class-weighted formulation are present identically in both versions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same multi-label node-classification task on PPI, PPI-large, Yelp, DBLP, OGBN-Proteins, PCG, HumanGo and EukaryoteGo. No datasets or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 5 retains Random, Herding and K-Center coreset methods, SGDD, GCDM, GCond and whole-dataset training. The corresponding adaptation comparisons, including probabilistic initialization, also retain the same participants.

E3.justification: Dataset splits in Table 1, condensation rates, F1-micro/F1-macro metrics and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Sections 5–6 and the appendix introduce no revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same initialization, structure-learning and loss-function comparisons, label-correlation and class-distribution analyses, and class-weighted optimization experiments in Section 6.2 and Appendix A.

E5.justification: Both retain point-estimate reporting without experimental repeat or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted findings in Tables 2–10 and Figures 2–7 are unchanged. For example, Table 5 retains GCond's PPI scores of 51.35 F1-micro and 23.86 F1-macro at 1.00% condensation. Apparent Yelp differences in sorted text extraction do not occur in the actual table rows.

T1.justification: Equations 1–30 retain the same definitions and mathematical formulations, including condensation objectives, label-correlation definitions and class-weighted losses. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about adapting graph condensation to multi-label datasets and the general effectiveness of GCond with K-Center initialization and BCELoss.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning structure preservation, label complexity and dataset-dependent performance are unchanged. The discussion of SGDD's out-of-memory limitations on Yelp and OGBN-Proteins is also retained.

D1.justification: The dataset-processing descriptions, experimental settings and Algorithm 1 provide the same technical information. No implementation details, hyperparameter values, hardware information or code/data access instructions are added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography and the positioning relative to existing graph-condensation and multi-label methods are unchanged. No cited works or novelty claims are added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, 23 Dec 2024, to v2, 4 Dec 2025. This is a limited administrative text update; the title, authors, prose, headings and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Small spacing and pagination changes occur on pages 9–10, including one line of Section 6 moving from page 10 to page 9. All ten tables, seven figures and Algorithm 1 retain their content and captions.

improvement.justification: The main text and Appendix A retain the same methods, evidence, mathematical formulations, interpretations and reproducibility information. The updated arXiv stamp and small layout adjustments provide no meaningful net change in scientific quality or readability.
